analysis:
The supplied units are head-text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 2026-2840). The recorded changed range is head 3541-3575, a new section on cluster service listeners following the cable and pairing. That range lies outside the supplied excerpts, and the patch excerpt is truncated. Only documentation changed in this file and no executable code changed. The excerpts I examined are unchanged surrounding text, covering MTP acceptance, sampling defaults, constrained Qwen JSON, tool parsers, vision caps, the MiMo native path and Flash-Next.

I found no regression in the supplied lines. Relevant threat IDs touched by the surrounding text are T-041 (prefix cache: the doc states that sampler choice does not alter cache identity, and SSD checkpoint identity is unchanged) and TB-007 (inference engine). I identified no doc claim that weakens the cache scoping, TTL or HMAC posture.

The visible patch excerpt describes new cluster listener behavior: a pairing-keyed handshake that rejects a stale pairing, a 5-second listener check, and restarts on cable or pairing change. This is a new distributed-cluster surface (ClusterSetupLinkExchange, ClusterService) that the canonical threat model does not define, so it is new attack surface. This PR only documents it. A reviewer of the corresponding source files should check cluster authentication (pin comparison, edge secret handling) and the listener bind address. I could not verify those from the supplied lines, so I record that as an unverified contract and not as a finding.

A pass over the complete patch and any associated code diffs, which are not in this batch, should examine the cluster listener trust boundary. It could warrant a new threat-model entry, because TB-002 through TB-013 do not cover local-cable cluster peers.
